apps.name: OKX
apps.note: Repcz/SukkaW currently have no preferred maintained dedicated OKX source. v2fly is used because its current OKX dataset is materially more complete and actively maintained than the old blackmatrix7 Surge list.

apps.name: WhatsApp
apps.note: v2fly is preferred over the older blackmatrix7 list because its current WhatsApp domain coverage is more modern and avoids relying on stale IP ranges or overly broad shared Meta endpoints.

apps.name: LINE
apps.note: v2fly currently provides more precise LINE coverage than the old blackmatrix7 list. Broad shared domains must be reviewed rather than inherited blindly. nhncorp.jp should remain under review but should not be excluded without evidence.

apps.name: GitHub
apps.note: v2fly is selected because the GitHub dataset is actively maintained and includes modern GitHub assets and related services. build.py must resolve v2fly include directives deliberately and must not import unrelated npm, Microsoft, Amazon, Azure, or other shared infrastructure merely because it is reachable through an include.

apps.name: SafePal
apps.note: Repcz, SukkaW, blackmatrix7, and MetaCubeX currently have no dedicated SafePal dataset. v2fly is selected because its actively maintained, narrowly scoped list contains both isafepal.com and safepal.com without include directives or attribute-qualified entries.

apps.name: PayPal
apps.note: Repcz is selected by the long-term source preference because its native Surge PayPal list currently normalizes to the same output as blackmatrix7. It is parsed as a policy-free native Surge source; no supplement is justified without a confirmed upstream gap.

apps.name: Netflix
apps.note: blackmatrix7 is selected because its native Surge list retains materially broader IPv4 and IPv6 coverage than the smaller domain-oriented v2fly dataset. build.py preserves its policy-free IP-CIDR no-resolve semantics; no supplement is justified without a confirmed upstream gap.

apps.name: YouTube
apps.note: Repcz is selected because its actively refreshed native Surge list keeps a compact set of core YouTube, video, image, API, and country-domain coverage. Its focused scope is preferred over larger lists whose extra entries do not provide confirmed value for this personal Rule-Set. The DOMAIN-SUFFIX,youtube.com entry also covers YouTube TV (tv.youtube.com), so no separate YouTube TV app is needed for the friend usage scenario.

apps.name: X
apps.note: Repcz is selected because its native X/Twitter list is actively refreshed, includes current X, Twitter, Grok, media, and focused IP coverage, and is a strict practical superset of the compared v2fly domain output without requiring format conversion.

apps.name: Instagram
apps.note: Repcz is selected for its compact first-party Instagram scope. The native DOMAIN-KEYWORD,instagram rule is excluded because it could route unrelated third-party domains; the remaining suffix rules cover instagram.com, cdninstagram.com, and instagr.am. v2fly is not selected because its larger dataset includes many unrelated follower, marketing, typo, and SEO domains.

apps.name: Telegram
apps.note: SukkaW is selected because its actively maintained native Surge source is limited to core Telegram domains and fits the preferred source tier. Repcz currently includes unsupported IP-ASN rules plus third-party client and telemetry scope; v2fly adds TON and related ecosystem domains that are not required for a conservative Telegram default. A supplemental IP source (ruleset.skk.moe/List/ip/telegram.conf, official Telegram CIDR list, 2026-08-13) is added so the canonical set carries both the domain (non-IP) and IP phases, enabling Blink to split Telegram into a non-IP view and an IP view for the Rule-layer multi-view pilot (2026-08).

apps.name: Threads
apps.note: Repcz and SukkaW currently provide no dedicated Threads Rule-Set. v2fly is selected because its small data file contains only threads.com and threads.net, needs no include expansion, and converts safely to Surge.

apps.name: TikTok
apps.note: Repcz is selected because its native TikTok list is actively refreshed and covers TikTok domains, ByteDance CDNs, keywords, and IP ranges more completely than every compared candidate. Its two IP-ASN entries are dropped through an explicit type-level exclude because build.py v1 does not emit ASN rules. blackmatrix7 is stale and drifts into ByteDance AI IDE domains; v2fly's TikTok entries all carry negative attributes that v1 refuses to interpret.

apps.name: Spotify
apps.note: Repcz is selected because it publishes a compact, actively refreshed, native Surge Spotify list that stays entirely inside the build.py v1 whitelist. SukkaW only embeds Spotify rules inside stream.ts (last changed 2025-11) and publishes them merged with other services; blackmatrix7 is about 14 months stale, and v2fly would import the third-party conductrics.com experiment host.

apps.name: AI
apps.note: Repcz AI.list is the aggregated mainstream-AI Rule-Set: it is an actively refreshed derivative of SukkaW's ai.conf plus the OpenAI file CDN oaiusercontent.com. The single URL-REGEX entry (the google.com/sorry Gemini continuation fix that requires MitM of www.google.com) is dropped through an explicit type-level exclude because build.py v1 does not emit URL-REGEX rules. DeepSeek is intentionally absent (domestic service, direct by default); it may only enter via a log-confirmed supplement.

apps.name: ZABank
apps.note: The 2026-08-15 source audit verified that Repcz, SukkaW, v2fly, blackmatrix7, and MetaCubeX provide no ZABank rules, so this app is supplement-only: the output is built exclusively from the repo-maintained supplement, whose three root domains (za.group, zainvest.group, zajourney.com) cover all nine candidate domains recorded from actual usage. build.py v1 allows an empty sources list for exactly this case.

apps.name: Steam
apps.note: Repcz is selected because its native, actively refreshed Steam list keeps a compact set of core Steam domains (store, community, chat, content, steamdeck) without CDN-specific or China-specific hosts, so it builds with zero conversion and no type-level excludes. SukkaW has no dedicated Steam rules. v2fly's dataset adds legacy regional CDNs and China entries; blackmatrix7 is stale and even includes the unrelated steamunlocked.net domain.

apps.name: APTV
apps.note: APTV (planned as "Live") is a personal live-streaming Rule-Set watched through the APTV frontend app. It is supplement-only by design: the rules are maintained by the repository owner (originally kept in a private list; migrated on 2026-08-15), contain no subscription URLs or tokens, and are not upstream-audited. Others reusing this repository should evaluate and replace these rules as needed.

apps.name: Disney
apps.note: Repcz is selected because its actively refreshed native Surge Disney list covers Disney+ streaming together with the Disney family brands (ABC, ESPN, National Geographic). PROCESS-NAME entries are dropped explicitly for Egern/Quantumult X and counted in the build report; the byte- identical classical output retains the line, which Loon and Shadowrocket simply ignore because the type does not exist there. No supplement is justified without a confirmed gap.

apps.name: ParamountPlus
apps.note: The 2026-08-16 audit found blackmatrix7 to be the only dedicated Paramount+ source (Repcz, SukkaW, v2fly, and MetaCubeX have none). Its Surge-native list covers paramountplus.com plus CBS streaming hosts and a focused USER-AGENT rule. It is about 14 months old, but the domains are stable; revisit if usage reveals missing hosts.

apps.name: Hulu
apps.note: blackmatrix7 is selected because its Surge-native Hulu list (US and JP scope) is the freshest dedicated source: the v2fly dataset is unchanged since 2022 and Repcz/SukkaW publish no standalone Hulu Rule-Set. The single PROCESS-NAME entry is dropped explicitly for Egern/Quantumult X and counted in the build report; the classical output retains the line for Loon/Shadowrocket, which ignore the unsupported type.

apps.name: PrimeVideo
apps.note: Repcz is selected because its actively refreshed native Surge list keeps core Prime Video domains plus exact, distribution-specific CloudFront and Akamai host entries, so no shared CDN namespace is swallowed. blackmatrix7 is older and adds a broader keyword; no supplement is justified without a confirmed upstream gap.

apps.name: HBO
apps.note: Repcz is selected because its actively refreshed native Surge list covers the HBO Max brand (hbomax.com and the current max.com) plus HBO-specific Akamai and CloudFront hosts. The two generic AWS API Gateway region suffixes are excluded explicitly: they would otherwise route unrelated AWS services, and the exclusion stays auditable in this manifest.

apps.name: Twitch
apps.note: blackmatrix7 is selected because its Surge-native list combines Twitch domains, a keyword, and no-resolve IP ranges (IPv4 and IPv6) into the most complete coverage. v2fly is fresher (2026-05) but domain-only, and Repcz/SukkaW publish no dedicated Twitch Rule-Set. The PROCESS-NAME entry is dropped explicitly for Egern/Quantumult X and counted in the build report; the classical output retains the line for Loon/ Shadowrocket, which ignore the unsupported type.

apps.name: Facebook
apps.note: Repcz is selected because its actively refreshed native Surge list keeps the widest current Facebook domain coverage, including the anti- typosquatting variants that are community-standard practice (the v2fly dataset carries the same kind of entries). No supplement is justified without a confirmed upstream gap.

apps.name: Google
apps.note: Repcz is selected because its actively refreshed native Surge list is a compact core for Google search and Gmail: DOMAIN-KEYWORD,google covers google.com and googleusercontent.com, and DOMAIN-KEYWORD,gmail covers gmail.com and googlemail.com. Unlike the Instagram keyword case, the google keyword is retained deliberately because it is the backbone of coverage and real third-party collisions are negligible. Its youtube.com entries deduplicate against the YouTube Rule-Set.

apps.name: NBA
apps.note: The 2026-08-16 audit found no NBA rules in Repcz, SukkaW, blackmatrix7, v2fly, MetaCubeX, or RuleGo, so this app is supplement-only: two root domains (nba.com, nba.net) cover the official site and the NBA app (api/cdn/stats subdomains live under nba.com). It stays supplement-only unless usage reveals missing hosts.

apps.name: Suno
apps.note: The 2026-08-16 audit found no Suno rules in any audited source, so this app is supplement-only: two root domains (suno.com, suno.ai) cover the web app, mobile app, and studio API. It stays supplement-only unless usage reveals missing hosts.

apps.name: Starryblu
apps.note: Starryblu is a global payment app (starryblu.com, Singapore FinTech exhibitor, App Store id 6736854716). The 2026-08-26 audit probed Repcz (Surge/Rules/Starryblu.list), SukkaW (Source/non_ip/starryblu.conf), v2fly (data/starryblu), and blackmatrix7 (rule/Surge/Starryblu) — all 404, no dedicated upstream, so this app is supplement-only: the root domain starryblu.com covers the official site and app API subdomains. It stays supplement-only unless usage reveals missing hosts.
